description:
Program Overview

The Dong Lab at Vanderbilt University, led by Dr. Xiaoguang Dong, is offering fully funded PhD positions in medical robotics and magnetic actuation. The lab focuses on developing miniature robots for surgical applications and catheter guidance systems using innovative magnetic actuation techniques.

Funding & Benefits

  • Tuition Fees: Full coverage for 4-5 years
  • Stipend: $34,000 - $38,000 per year (competitive) for 4-5 years
  • Health Insurance: Comprehensive coverage
  • Research Funding: Access to lab equipment and materials
  • Conference Travel: Funding for international conferences annually

Research Focus

  • Miniature Medical Robots: Developing small-scale robots for minimally invasive surgery
  • Magnetic Actuation: Creating magnetic systems for controlled movement inside the body
  • Biomedical Devices: Designing innovative medical devices for clinical applications
  • Soft Robotics: Creating flexible robots that can navigate biological environments
  • Catheter Guidance Systems: Developing advanced systems for vascular interventions

Eligibility Criteria

  • Academic Background: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Biomedical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field
  • Research Experience: Prior experience in robotics, medical devices, or magnetic systems (preferred but not required)
  • GPA: 3.5+ (on 4.0 scale) for competitive application
  • English Proficiency: TOEFL 90+ or IELTS 6.5+ (for international students)

Application Process

  1. Contact Dr. Dong with CV and research statement.
  2. Submit graduate application to Vanderbilt Engineering.
  3. Departmental review.
  4. Interview with lab members.
  5. Funding decision.
  6. Begin PhD program.

Required Documents

  • CV/Resume highlighting academic and research experience
  • Research Statement (2-3 pages)
  • Transcripts (all undergraduate and graduate records)
  • Three Letters of Recommendation
  • English Proficiency Scores (TOEFL or IELTS if applicable)

  • research on next-generation medical robots for minimally invasive surgery.

  • Guaranteed funding for 4-5 years through NIH and NSF grants.
  • Dr. Dong is an NIH R01 and R21 grant recipient.
